problem: With EN high, IN1 = IN2 = 0 makes both outputs low, which shorts the two motor terminals together and brakes the motor. It does not coast. Coasting needs the channel disabled (EN low), which makes the outputs high-impedance so no current can flow.
fix: Write: IN1 high with IN2 low turns the motor one way, swap them for the other way, and both inputs low brakes the motor to a fast stop. To coast, hold EN low so both outputs float. Quiz Q4 must repeat the brake/coast distinction.

problem: The wrong-way division N = 1.8°/360° gives 0.005 instead of 200, which is 40,000 times too small, not 200 times. The 200 is N itself, so the error factor is 200 × 200.
fix: Say: dividing the wrong way gives a step count 40,000 times too small, so every speed answer is wrong by the same huge factor.

problem: The ULN2003 already has internal freewheeling diodes, so leaving out an external diode does not by itself destroy a ULN2003 channel. Damage happens when the COM pin is left floating instead of being tied to the coil supply positive. The missing-diode warning applies to a discrete transistor switch.
fix: Say: an external diode is a must for a discrete transistor; for the ULN2003 the protection works only if COM is wired to the motor supply, so forgetting that wire is the equivalent mistake.

where: Section 1 (coils on P0.0 to P0.3) and Section 3 (base resistor design)
problem: Port 0 of the 8051 has open-drain outputs and needs external pull-up resistors (about 10 kΩ) before it can drive anything. Also, an 8051 pin sinks about 1.6 mA but sources only about 60 µA, so it cannot supply the 0.9 mA base current the section's own design asks for; a buffer or a ULN2003 input driven by a stronger pin is needed in practice.
fix: Add one line: Port 0 needs external 10 kΩ pull-ups to act as an output. Add one line in Section 3: the calculated base current is a few hundred microamps to about 1 mA, more than an 8051 pin can source, so a buffer such as a 74HC gate sits between the pin and R_B (or a relay module with an opto input is used).
